scope: TimerQueue advance with pending far-future timers; source-defined repeated minimum scans. Not an external-peer ranking or timing claim.
mechanism: advance previously reset cached next and rescanned every entry in the nearest untouched bucket even when no timer was due. Scheduler fire_due_timers calls this on busy worker dispatches with pending timers.
change: Reuse an unchanged still-future exact cached minimum; next_dirty remembers earliest cancellation so the next advance still refreshes it as documented. Existing origin/rebucket/delivery/cancel ownership rules remain.
state: One private bool uses existing Windows x64 tail padding: measured sizeof TimerQueue1080 and TimerEntry48 unchanged. No new allocation or public option. Other-platform layout/ABI and runtime not measured.
workload: 64/1024/16384 stable nodes at2^40+i,128 advances1..128, with and without cancelling the minimum before the first poll; verify exact next after every poll, now/count/no-early-fire and final full delivery.
metric: Source-instrumented recompute_next callback entry visits, same single increment in both scratch headers. Counter probes are not latency measurements or CPU instruction counts; no production tracing added.
tests: 27 TimerQueue tests passed on actual uninstrumented candidate header, including million-node randomized arm/cancel delivery, radix boundaries, cancellation/rearm, UINT64_MAX, pre-existing delivery-list contents and death/lifetime checks.
review: backend_assembly_design independently reviewed dirty/cancel/rearm/rebucket/MAX paths; no confirmed semantic issue. Preserve original next-advance cancellation refresh contract.
closure: MSVC14.50.35717 optimized O2/MD/W4/WX fresh probe/test TUs only; existing same-toolchain foundation/gtest reused, no configure or SDK copy/build. Header-only clients do not imply a rebuilt Scheduler runtime.
initial_failure: First standalone test link lacked SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE, LNK1561. Kept failure logs; added console subsystem only and linked existing test object, then ran tests once. run.py now has the successful link flag; finish_tests.py records the actual recovery.
limits: No Scheduler/IO latency, external Seastar comparison, other OS/ISA, whole-suite or full SDK rebuild. Cancellation of a current minimum may still require one nearest-bucket scan on the next advance.
